Overview - Alnico Deep Pot Magnets
When the shallow pot is not enough
A deep pot holds a taller magnet in a deeper steel shell. The field reaches further into the workpiece, so the pull on thick steel is higher than a shallow pot of the same diameter gives.

Deep pots are used for heavier clamping and fixtures in fabrication and machining, for holding tooling and jigs on steel frames, and near welding and heat treatment where the alnico core keeps its strength.

Overview - Alnico Power Magnets
The magnet for hot and steady work

Alnico is an alloy of aluminium, nickel and cobalt. It gives less pull than neodymium for the same size, and in return it keeps its strength close to heat and gives a field that hardly changes over the years.

That makes it the right choice for holding fixtures near welding and heat treatment, for instruments and sensors, and for test equipment. The threaded hole bolts the magnet straight to a plate or fixture.

Overview - Alnico Shallow Pot Magnets
A cup that multiplies the hold
The steel cup carries the field from the back of the magnet round to the working face. The pull on that face is several times what the bare magnet would give, and the magnet is protected from knocks.

Shallow pots suit thin plate and fixtures where height is limited. They hold jigs, guards, sensors, signs and tools, and hang cables and hoses from steel frames. A countersunk hole or a threaded stud bolts the magnet in place.

Which magnet for the job
Choose alnico where the magnet sits near a welding or heat treatment area, or where a very stable field matters, as in instruments and sensors.
Choose neodymium where the space is small and the pull must be high. Keep it below 80 degrees Celsius.

Choose a pot or channel magnet where the magnet is bolted to a fixture. The steel shell directs the field to one face and protects the magnet from knocks. Tell us the pull you need and the space you have, and we will pick the size.

Overview - Neodymium Block Magnets
The most pull in the least space

A neodymium block gives a strong, even field across a flat face. Blocks are used for clamping and fixtures, for holding sensors and covers, inside magnetic assemblies and separators, and wherever a small magnet must do a large job.
The plating protects the magnet from rust. Keep the working temperature below 80 degrees Celsius, as neodymium loses strength when hot. Standard sizes are stocked and other sizes are cut to order.

Overview - Neodymium Channel Magnet
Strong hold on one face
The steel channel wraps three sides of the magnet. It directs the field to the open face, so the pull on that face is higher than the bare magnet would give, and it protects the magnet from knocks.

Channel magnets hold signs, panels and covers on steel surfaces, mount fixtures in fabrication and assembly, and keep tools within reach in a workshop. Keep the working temperature below 80 degrees Celsius.
